1hic: short i (Lewis & Short hīc, haec, hōc, marking the heavy syllable as a long vowel). De Vaan 284, s.v. hic: the nominative is *hi-ke, so the vowel is short and the syllable heavy (hicc, p. 102, s.v. -ce); the adverb hīc, here, is the old locative *hoi-ke. As in the record for “current”.

hic1, haec, hoc

demonstrative pronoun and adjective; plural hī, hae, haec · Declension on Wiktionary

this; (plural) these

What is near the speaker, or what has just been said or is about to be. Beside ille it is “this … that”, and of two things just named, “the latter” (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • iste, ista, istud — this (that you have, by you)

    demonstrative pronoun and adjective · also used · classical · Mart. 4.49.10: laudant illa, sed ista legunt · Declension on Wiktionary

    The demonstrative of the person spoken to: English often says “this” of what the listener holds or has just said. See “that”.

Examples

  • Hoc facitō. — Rēctē sānē. — Hoc fugitō. — Callidē.

    Do this. — Quite right. — Avoid this. — Clever.Ter. Ad. 417

  • hoc, jūcunde, tibi poēma fēcī

    I made this poem for you, my dearCatull. 50.16

  • Haec est diēs quam fēcit Dominus; exsultēmus, et laetēmur in eā.

    This is the day which the Lord has made; let us rejoice and be glad in it.Vulg. Ps. 117 (118), 24

  • haec scrīpsī nāvigāns

    I wrote this on board shipCic. Att. 16.7.8

  • Bonō animō es: accēde ad ignem hunc; jam calēscēs plūs satis.

    Cheer up: come over to this fire; you’ll soon be more than warm enough.Ter. Eun. 84–85

  • hic tibi nocturnōs praestābit cēreus ignēs

    this wax candle will give you light at nightMart. 14.42.1

See also that, here, this one or that one?, same.
